correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired variance theorem on homogeneous independent cyclic priorities. A marked gap needs the excursion and two exterior guards. Sum the variance and covariances over relative offsets: on the line the only compatible dependent nonzero offsets are ±g (common valley) and ±(g+2) (one common guard). At K=2g+4 all diagrams with |h|≤g+1 have unwrapped windows covering at most K distinct sites. The two ±(g+2) offsets merge; the new diagram shares both guards. Replacing two covariances by one gives w−2v+a², including the independence reference exactly once. Conditioning on the four endpoints gives the trace with M,M, M,R or R,R, where M(s,t)=min(s,t) and R(s,t)=st; cycling the trace gives K_i(M−R)K_i(M−R). The bridge operator is positive injective with complete sine eigenbasis, so its square root has dense range. Nonzero symmetric Hilbert–Schmidt K_i cannot have zero sandwich; the trace is its squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm. This proves strict positivity, not merely nonnegativity. The companion mean boundary is the published shared-guard integral; integrating on s=ut<t gives the asserted value, and the zero regime follows from separation on both arcs.
residual_risks: Finite computations verify selected cases only. The operator proof is necessary for all i and does not cover smaller cycle variances or mixed gap lengths.
